bends.reason: bend_01.png: the scan outline follows the blue FORMED profile through the bend radius and along the whole ~10 mm flange to its free end. There are no scan points on the orange NOT FORMED leg. Corroborated by: (1) the far end of the bend_02.png section (B1 side), where the scan follows the formed flange including its radius; (2) overlay SIDE, where the CAD B1 post is fully covered by scan points; (3) overlay TOP and raw TOP, which show the flange edge-on as a dark double line along the full B1 edge; (4) raw SIDE, where one long-edge flange turns about 90 deg. Formed in the recipe direction, to the side of the base opposite B3; not reversed. The CAD is mirror-symmetric about its long centre plane, so the B1 (not B2) assignment rests on the display registration (confidence OK). It agrees with an independent handedness check of the raw views against the CAD views: with B3's end and direction fixed, a proper rotation puts the formed long flange on B1's edge.

bend_02.png: the scan outline runs straight on from the parent flange along the orange NOT FORMED profile, so the flange is coplanar with the base. There are no scan points on the blue FORMED leg, and none on the opposite (reverse-bend) side, so this is flat, not reverse-formed. Corroborated by: (1) the far end of the bend_01.png section (B2 side), which is flat; (2) overlay TOP and ISO, where the scan carries on flat about 7-8 mm past the B2 bend line along the full length, with a chamfered relief corner at the B3 end, while the CAD's formed B2 flange shows only as faint surface with no scan on it; (3) overlay SIDE, where the CAD B2 post is empty and the scan's base extends past it; (4) raw TOP and SIDE, where the base is wider on that side, with no edge-on flange and no post. The region is densely scanned, so it is determinable. This makes the part out of recipe sequence: B3 (seq 3) is formed while B2 (seq 2) is not.

bend_03.png: the scan follows the blue FORMED profile, a ~20 mm end flange at about 90 deg, and the orange leg is empty. The raw views show the end flange clearly formed at about 90 deg: an edge-on bar at the end in TOP, and its face in FRONT, SIDE and ISO. It is identified as B3 by hole spacing: the holes sit at about 0.49 and 0.65 of the length from that end, as in the CAD, and the opposite end carries the tab. B3 is the recipe's reverse-direction bend: in the CAD it goes to the opposite side of the base from B1 and B2. The scan's end flange is likewise on the side opposite its formed long flange (raw SIDE) and matches the FORMED reference in the overlay, so it is formed in the recipe direction, not reversed.
